tldr: Fixing two latent confounder types can create an ALTTE efficiency gain that vanishes once regularity is required over a model admitting one additional positive type. At every positive separated binary law with strict public bridge slack, four observationally equivalent ternary splits jointly span the full \(31\)-dimensional outcome-moment tangent, so the at-most-three-type efficiency bound equals the Chen--Xie moment bound even though each single ternary Jacobian has rank only \(28\). A finite binary reconstruction and projection gives the exact observable cliff criterion \(\Delta>0\). The occupied exact witness certifies a nonempty relatively open strict-cliff region. A total, data-only two-step generalized least-squares estimator targets \(\tau_M\) on the finite outcome-moment class, uses the exact finite-stratum influence function \(\phi_{M,n}\), and has uniform normal-approximation error \(O(\log n/\sqrt n)\) on compact regular classes. The categorical structural subclass is a least-favorable certificate for the broader Chen--Xie Section 5 model: the converse transfers upward, while their attaining upper bound completes that larger-class comparison. No claim is made that the finite-cell estimator covers their continuous-spline application.
gap: Chen and Xie derive the observable outcome-moment ALTTE bound, and the occupied fixed-binary proposal derives a smaller structural projection, but neither determines the tangent seen by estimators that must remain regular when a positive third latent type is allowed. Budanova's oracle result requires identification of a parsimonious mixture and therefore does not answer the same-law split problem.
fill: The project proves universal four-split score saturation on the separated binary stratum, derives the exact observed projection-residual criterion, and supplies a total moment-efficient estimator whose expansion uses the exact finite allocation \(\rho_n\). The observable functional \(\tau_M\) is defined on the relaxation, and equality with the causal ALTTE is asserted only on structural laws.
